statement: You are given a binary tree with distinct values, and two values p and q that are both in the tree. The tree is given as the array tree in level order, indexed from 0: the root is tree[0], and the left and right children of the node at index i are at indices 2i + 1 and 2i + 2. null marks a position with no node, and every position below a null must be null too.
The lowest common ancestor of two nodes is the deepest node that has both of them in its subtree. A node counts as being in its own subtree, so a node can be the ancestor of itself.
Return the value of the lowest common ancestor of the nodes holding p and q.

examples.explanation: 7 and 4 are the two children of 2 (indices 9 and 10), so 2 is the deepest node above both.
4 lies in the subtree of 5, and 5 is an ancestor of itself, so the answer is 5.

constraints: p and q are both in the tree.
